correction.text: unchanged shape (Honshu, Shikoku and Kyushu), but for 1333-1336 only: 'a three-year period of Imperial rule' that ended when 'On February 25, 1336, Ashikaga Takauji entered the capital'

keyframe_review.note: Years only: Cliopatria runs the Kenmu label to 1343, seven years past the end the page gives, and the Ashikaga row starts in 1344; 1336-1343 is carried by the new ashikaga-shogunate_1336 keyframe on the same outline. The infobox gives no area, so no area check; the 320,516 km2 outline equals the Kamakura row's and is the realm claimed, not the ground held: Hōjō Tokiyuki beat Tadayoshi in Musashi, Prince Narinaga was installed with Tadayoshi as 'de facto ruler', and Prince Norinaga was sent to Mutsu (both undated on the page).

region.text: the capital region around Heian-kyō, seat of the restored imperial government

ledger.note: 1333: Go-Daigo's Kenmu Restoration begins at Kyoto. The page dates the regime 'a three-year period of Imperial rule' from 1333 and the 'Siege of Kamakura: May 18, 1333'; the Hōjō garrison at Rokuhara was destroyed in 1333. The page gives no day for the court's return to Kyoto.

1333: the Kamakura realm passes to the restored imperial government. The page: samurai from the western manors had 'defeated the shogunate' for Go-Daigo and the city of Kamakura was 'finally reached, besieged, and taken' (18 May 1333). The page names no provinces; the realm is Cliopatria's Kamakura outline (identical to its Kenmu outline).

region.text: Kamakura and the Kantō, where Tadayoshi ruled for his brother, and the capital region Takauji entered on 25 February 1336

ledger.note: 1335: the Ashikaga break with the court. 'On November 17, 1335, Tadayoshi issued a message in his brother's name'; that year Hōjō Tokiyuki had defeated Tadayoshi in Musashi and Tadayoshi, fleeing Kamakura, had ordered Prince Morinaga beheaded. The page does not say what the message ordered; it is read here as the start of Takauji's revolt, with the Kantō as the zone.

region.text: Kamakura and the Kantō, where Tadayoshi ruled for his brother, and the capital region Takauji entered on 25 February 1336

ledger.note: 1336: Takauji enters the capital and the Kenmu Restoration ends. 'On February 25, 1336, Ashikaga Takauji entered the capital and the Kenmu Restoration ended' (infobox: 'Ashikaga Takauji captures Kyoto: February 23 1336'). [Reviewer 2026-10-18: confidence 3 to 2; the page names the capital, not the Kantō part of the zone.]

region.text: the realm of the restored imperial government

ledger.note: 1336: the Kenmu Restoration ends with Takauji's entry into Kyoto. The page puts the end of the restoration on 25 February 1336; Go-Daigo himself 'escaped from the capital in January 1337' to found the Southern Court at Yoshino (Nanboku-chō page), and the Ashikaga shogunate is dated 11 August 1336.

wars.name: Genkō War
wars.outcome: Go-Daigo's side won: the Hōjō garrison at Rokuhara was destroyed in 1333 and Kamakura fell on 18 May 1333, ending the shogunate.
wars.note: The page dates the war inconsistently: infobox 'Genkō War begins: 1333', body 'launched the Genkō War in 1331'. The Kamakura dossier carries the matching contest events from 1331. [Reviewer 2026-10-18: from 1331 to 1333 to keep the war inside the regime's life (infobox: Genkō War begins: 1333); the 1331-1333 fighting is in the kamakura-shogunate dossier.]

wars.name: Ashikaga Takauji's rebellion against the Kenmu government

wars.outcome: Takauji entered the capital on 25 February 1336 and the Kenmu Restoration ended; the Ashikaga shogunate was established on 11 August 1336 and Go-Daigo withdrew to Yoshino in January 1337.
wars.note: Battles of the winter and spring of 1336 (including the Battle of Minatogawa) are not on the page; the page gives Tadayoshi's 17 November 1335 message and the 23/25 February 1336 entry.

certainty.note: A three-year regime with no surveyed frontier; the outline is the Kamakura realm Cliopatria carries over, and rule outside the capital region was contested.

notes:
Written by Phase B agent jk-01-b on 2026-10-18 from two pages (budget 1-2). The Kenmu page's own dates are inconsistent in places (Genkō War 1331 vs 1333; the era counted 1334-1336 by Southern Court reckoning and 1334-1338 by the Northern Court); the dossier follows the page's 'three-year period of Imperial rule' 1333-1336 and the 25 February 1336 end.

Cliopatria: one shape 1333-1343 (320,516 km2, the Kamakura outline); the regime ended in February 1336 and Cliopatria's Ashikaga row starts in 1344, so 1336-1343 is given to the Ashikaga dossier as a new keyframe (ashikaga-shogunate_1336). The infobox has no area.

Not settled: the Minatogawa battle, Takauji's retreat to Kyushu and return, the Kamakura-fu under Prince Narinaga and Tadayoshi and the Mutsu command under Prince Norinaga are on the page only without years; no events are written for them. Where the Kenmu court really governed (the Kinai, parts of the west) is not on the page.

Needs a dossier from another group: southern-court (the Southern Court at Yoshino, 1337-1392), successor of this regime's court line; its land is a handful of mountain districts around Yoshino. The gazetteer lacks the place 'Yoshino' (Yoshino mountains, Nara Prefecture, about 34.37 N 135.86 E).
